assignment.acceptance_condition: A proved lower bound N(H) >= g(H) with explicit constants, including exact analysis of the chain recurrence and, for any subtree argument, proved lower bounds on distinct children per vertex and proved upper bounds on per-level height growth; if only a logarithmic bound is provable, a precise statement of what blocks the power bound.
assignment.objective: From first principles, prove the strongest rigorous lower bound attainable for N(H). Construct explicit infinite families of solutions with controlled height growth and prove their members are distinct: at minimum a single chain (e.g., (1,1,1,3) -> (1,1,3,11) -> (1,1,11,41) -> ... generated by repeatedly mutating the second-largest coordinate) giving N(H) >= c log H with an explicit constant from the chain's growth rate (analyze the associated linear recurrence exactly); then attack a power lower bound N(H) >= c H^alpha by exhibiting a subtree in which every vertex has at least 2 (or more) provably distinct children whose maxima grow by a bounded factor per level, and determine the best provable alpha. If a power bound cannot be proved, identify the precise obstruction (e.g., inability to control the growth factor along branching edges, or collisions between children). All families must be proved to consist of solutions (direct substitution into a^2+b^2+c^2+d^2 = 4abcd) and proved distinct.
assignment.rationale: D5 is an independent obligation from D4; lower bounds require constructive family arguments of a different character than tree-counting upper bounds, so it runs as its own thread.

context.product_intent: This run tests mathematical discovery and proof, not research composition: the memorandum exists to establish from first principles, with complete proofs, what is true about the Markov-Hurwitz n=4 mutation graph and the growth of solution counts N(H), with theorems cleanly separated from labeled, reproducible observations and from conjecture. Honest partial progress with clearly stated obstructions — and no assumed growth law — is the explicit acceptance standard, so the product's value lies in rigor and in identifying the most informative next mathematical step.
stable_context: SC1: S is the set of sorted positive-integer quadruples (a,b,c,d), 1 <= a <= b <= c <= d, satisfying a^2+b^2+c^2+d^2 = 4abcd (raw request).
SC2: A Vieta mutation replaces one coordinate x_i by 4 times the product of the other three coordinates minus x_i, followed by sorting; permutations are identified (raw request).
SC3: The request designates (1,1,1,1) as the root; substitution gives 4 = 4, so it lies in S.
SC4: N(H) denotes the number of sorted solutions with maximum coordinate at most H (raw request).

context.task: Investigate the mutation graph of sorted positive-integer solutions of a^2+b^2+c^2+d^2 = 4abcd under Vieta mutation. First prove or refute the structural claims — connectivity of every solution to (1,1,1,1), uniqueness of a height-decreasing mutation at every non-root vertex, and the consequent rooted-tree structure of the quotient graph — then pursue the open asymptotic part: strongest attainable rigorous upper and lower bounds for N(H), the relation between mutation depth and log H, an active search for exceptional small solutions, hidden cycles, multiple parents, and induction failure modes, and sharply separated conjectures. Deliver a self-contained research memorandum.
context.title: Markov-Hurwitz equation a^2+b^2+c^2+d^2=4abcd: Vieta-mutation graph structure and growth of N(H)
